text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: us-west1 egress gateway elevated 5xx rate detected. 5xx rate = 7.2% over last 3m (baseline 0.2%). Error breakdown: 502 proxy_exhaust, 504 upstream_timeout. Triggering page to on-call. Logs: /alerts/1769876543
erica: oncall here, seeing the page. what's the current customer impact?
sam: I have a dashboard up — rps hasn't spiked, but tail latency and 5xx are up for streaming and long-context jobs. Impacting ~18% of requests from west coast users.
zara: grabbing gateway logs now. pattern: connections to a subset of edgepool nodes returning ECONNRESET and http 502. Possibly proxy thread saturation.
erica: can we triage whether this is infra saturation or a routing regression? any deploys?
matt: no prod deploys in the last 30m. Last deploy was 42m ago, checked deploy-bot.
sam: quick health checks:
```
# probe a couple of gateway nodes
curl -I https://gw-us-west1-01.redwood-inference.internal/health
# sample stream request to model-router
curl -s -N -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" -d '{"input":"hello"}' https://api.redwood.com/v1/streams | head
```
sam: probes show intermittent connection resets from gw-us-west1-0{1,2}. responses either hang then 504 or immediate 502.
zara: logs snippet:
```
2026-03-15T16:05:12Z gw-us-west1-01 proxy: read error: connection reset by peer
2026-03-15T16:05:13Z gw-us-west1-02 router: upstream timeout to ml-worker-12 (kv-cache miss)
2026-03-15T16:06:02Z gw-us-west1-04 proxy: accept queue full, dropping connection
```
erica: looks like edgeproxy queueing + some worker upstream slowdowns. we should open a short mitigation window: 1) reroute traffic away from affected edgepool nodes, 2) enable cross-region spill to us-east1 for affected routes, 3) scale pool if needed.
sre-lead: agree. I recommend immediate traffic steering + dropping long-tail sessions to reduce queue pressure. We'll do gradual shift: 20% -> 50% -> 100% if metrics clear. also enable circuit-breaker fallback for streaming routes.
matt: I'll start changing routing weights. doing a small shift to us-east1 now (weight change via control-plane API).
```
# pseudo commands
POST /api/v1/routing/policies/steer
{"policy":"region_preference","from":"us-west1","to":"us-east1","weight":0.2,"note":"emergency spill due to gw errors"}
```
matt: applied 20% spill to us-east1. monitoring...
sam: 3m after shift: 5xx dropped from 7.2% -> 4.1% overall, requests latency median stable but p95 still elevated.
erica: good. increase to 60% and concurrently scale the gw-us-west1 edgepool nodes by +2.
matt: scaling edgepool group 'gw-us-west1-ep' via infra API:
```
POST /infra/edgepools/gw-us-west1-ep/scale
{"delta":2,"graceful":true}
```
matt: scale request accepted, new instances launching.
zara: adding temporary ACL to prevent new long-lived streaming sessions from landing in the problematic nodes: enabling short-timeout policy for streaming routes in west region.
sam: also toggled prefix KV-cache enable to reduce upstream load for repeated prompts.
erica: support-team please draft a status update for status.redwood.ai — mention partial degradation for west coast users and ongoing remediation.
support-team: drafting: "We are investigating elevated 5xx and timeouts affecting a subset of west-coast API requests. Traffic is being rerouted to alternate region while we mitigate. Some streaming sessions may experience failures. More updates in 15 minutes"
erica: good. also send a targeted note to customers with SLA contracts using us-west region (cc: account execs).
sre-lead: monitoring shows error rate at 1.1% after scaling and 60% spill. p95 latency improved from 820ms -> 320ms. still seeing occasional 502s tied to a single host gw-us-west1-02.
zara: isolating host gw-us-west1-02 from load balancer, marking draining.
sam: confirming: after draining 02, 5xx dropped to 0.6% overall. rollover looks healthy.
erica: excellent. we'll leave cross-region spill at 40% for the next 30m while we validate stability and let scaled nodes warm caches. then we'll slowly shift back.
matt: documenting actions performed:
- applied emergency routing policy to spill traffic to us-east1 (20% -> 60% -> 40%)
- scaled gw-us-west1-ep by +2 instances
- drained gw-us-west1-02 from LB
- enabled short-session timeouts for streaming in us-west1
- toggled prefix KV-cache on for hot routes
erica: post-incident asks: run root-cause analysis on why accept queue got full on those proxies; look at connection handling and upstream backpressure; validate autoscaler thresholds for edgepool; add synthetic tests for long-stream sessions from west coast.
sre-lead: agreed. schedule follow-up postmortem with infra and runtime teams. assigned to zara and sam for initial RCA.
sam: I'll capture a timeline + graphs for the postmortem.
zara: will pull core dumps and proxy thread metrics from gw-us-west1-02.
ersupport: (support-team) we've posted the status update and notified enterprise customers.
erica: handing off to night oncall: @matt will take follow-up until 22:00 PST. leave spill at 40% and watch 5xx < 1% for 30m. next steps in summary message to follow. :wave: 
matt: acknowledged, I'll monitor dashboards and escalate if we see >1% 5xx or p95 > 500ms.
incident-bot: incident update saved to /incidents/1769876543, severity: SEV2, customer-impact: regional partial degradation (us-west1), pager: oncall-erica -> matt (handoff).
erica: quick note for postmortem: include mitigation timeline, config diffs (routing + edgepool scale), and customer communication copy. tagging @sre-lead for final review. :thumbsup:
